sections.overview: This rock-dwelling iguana is endemic to southwestern Madagascar.
sections.identification: It has a flattened body, fine keeled scales and a blue-grey back.
sections.habitat: It uses rocky or limestone outcrops and nearby thorn scrub.
sections.diet: The regional species account reports an insect diet.
sections.reproduction: It lays eggs; a regional account reports clutches of four to six.
sections.ecology: The Reptile Database places it in arid southwestern Madagascar, including the Fiherenana and Onilahy valleys.
sections.conservation: A regional guide lists habitat loss and degradation as threats and reports Least Concern; this is not a new assessment.
